discovery: Programmable quantum matter with arrays of individually trapped Rydberg atoms

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation and quantum information
motivation: The nominees turned single neutral atoms, held in optical tweezers and coupled through strong Rydberg interactions, into a controllable platform for quantum many-body physics and quantum information. Saffman proposed and demonstrated Rydberg-blockade entangling gates between individual atoms. Browaeys showed blockade and coherent excitation exchange between two atoms, then built defect-free, reconfigurable arrays in one, two and three dimensions. Lukin, with collaborators, used large programmable arrays to observe quantum phase transitions, many-body scars and topological spin liquids, and recently to run error-corrected logical qubits. Starting from basic atomic physics, the work has become a tool used in condensed-matter physics, quantum optics and computation, with direct measurement of quantum states atom by atom. It shows how precise control of light and atoms opens new frontiers in physics, as laser cooling and trapping did before it.
